extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR units, power plant environmental compliance staff, environmental consultants, and regulatory attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements, definitions, and compliance steps for legacy coal combustion residual (CCR) surface impoundments under the final EPA rule, including which existing 40 CFR part 257, subpart D requirements apply, tailored requirements for units closed by removal or with waste in place, and compliance deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure-by-removal completion standard (§257.102(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure is complete when all CCR has been removed from the CCR unit, any areas affected by releases from the CCR unit have been removed, and groundwater monitoring concentrations do not exceed the groundwater protection standard in §257.95(h) for Appendix IV constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To meet §257.102(c), the facility must remove all CCR and any impacted areas, and demonstrate via groundwater monitoring that Appendix IV constituent concentrations do not exceed the groundwater protection standard (either the MCL or background). This standard is used to determine whether closure by removal is complete for certifications and applicability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of closure by removal for legacy CCR surface impoundments
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility that completed closure by removal before the effective date but that contained CCR and liquids on October 19, 2015 may be required only to post documentation on the facility's CCR website that it has met the standards in §257.102(c) for that unit (i.e., the certification of closure by removal for legacy CCR surface impoundments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible for the closure certification, the facility must document that (consistent with existing standards) all CCR has been removed, any areas affected by releases removed, and have groundwater monitoring data demonstrating concentrations of each Appendix IV constituent do not exceed the relevant groundwater protection standard (MCL or background) for two consecutive sampling events. If a facility certifies all legacy CCR surface impoundments on-site meet §257.102(c) before the effective date, the facility is not subject to further legacy or CCRMU requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of legacy CCR surface impoundment (presence-date rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility that initiated closure by removal prior to October 19, 2015, but whose impoundment still contained CCR and liquids on or after October 19, 2015 is considered a legacy CCR surface impoundment and regulated under the final rule, even if the facility removed all CCR prior to the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some individual requirements may no longer be applicable if the impoundment completes closure before the compliance date applicable to a given requirement; but the presence of CCR and liquids on or after October 19, 2015 makes the unit a legacy CCR surface impoundment for applicability purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of existing 40 CFR part 257, subpart D requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing that, in most cases, existing requirements in 40 CFR part 257, subpart D applicable to inactive CCR surface impoundments apply to legacy CCR surface impoundments, except for the location restrictions at §§257.60–257.64 and the liner design criteria at §257.71.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA has limited discretion to establish requirements significantly different from those for inactive impoundments; therefore, most existing subpart D requirements apply. Commenters' suggestions for many new/expanded requirements (zero discharge, new financial assurance, etc.) were not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions: non-CCR impoundments
rubrics_metrics.description: Units generally referred to as cooling water ponds, process water ponds, wastewater treatment ponds, storm water holding ponds, or aeration ponds do not meet the definition of a CCR surface impoundment and therefore are not legacy impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's 2015 guidance explained these units are not designed to hold an accumulation of CCR and treatment/storage/disposal of accumulated CCR does not occur in these units. Misidentification in proposal corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: New/modified groundwater monitoring approach (combined detection and assessment monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: For legacy CCR surface impoundments EPA is combining detection and assessment monitoring (a revision of existing groundwater monitoring requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change affects how groundwater monitoring and corrective action are implemented for legacy impoundments (applies to both closed-by-removal and closed-with-waste-in-place subsets where monitoring is required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability documentation/reporting requirement (§257.100(f)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments are subject to a new applicability documentation requirement (reporting requirement) to demonstrate applicability/status under the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must prepare the specified applicability report to establish that a unit is subject to the legacy impoundment requirements or to document eligibility for tailored subsets (e.g., closed by removal). The final rule includes an applicability documentation metric as one of the legacy-impoundment-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site security requirement (§257.100(f)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments are subject to a new site security requirement to restrict public access to these sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site security is intended to minimize unauthorized entry of people or animals that could disturb final covers or monitoring equipment; applies to legacy impoundments that still contain CCR or waste in place. EPA determined site security was not relevant for units that had closed by removal and where land is repurposed, though protection of monitoring equipment is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored subset of requirements for units closed by removal prior to effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments that completed closure by removal before the effective date but cannot complete certification must comply with: the applicability report, installation of a permanent marker, all groundwater monitoring and corrective action (including combined detection and assessment monitoring), recordkeeping, notification, and website posting. If a CCRMU is discovered onsite during Facility Evaluation Report (FER) activities, the owner/operator must develop a fugitive dust control plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA determined other design/operational criteria (e.g., EAP, weekly inspections) are not applicable when CCR is no longer present. Site security requirement generally not applied to closed-by-removal subset, but monitoring equipment must be protected. Fugitive dust plan required only if CCRMU is discovered; timeline for plan completion tied to FER schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored subset of requirements for units closed with waste in place prior to effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments that have completed closure with waste in place (or closure eligible for deferral to permitting) must comply with: applicability report, site security, permanent marker, history of construction, fugitive dust control plan, annual fugitive dust control report, all groundwater monitoring and corrective action (including combined detection and assessment monitoring), written post-closure care plan, post-closure care, recordkeeping, notification, and website posting; plus provide information and supporting documentation demonstrating closure meets §257.102(d) or §257.101(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explained why many other design/operating criteria are not applicable (e.g., inflow design flood control system plan, periodic hazard/structural assessments) because units have installed a final cover and require post-closure care and monitoring instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fugitive dust control plan and annual report
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must prepare a fugitive dust control plan (and annual fugitive dust control report where required) for legacy CCR surface impoundments subject to CCRMU requirements or when CCRMU is discovered onsite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even units unlikely to generate fugitive dust (closed units) must prepare plans because CCRMU activities (field work, closures) can generate dust. If CCRMU discovered onsite of a facility with a legacy impoundment that closed by removal, the owner/operator must complete a fugitive dust plan no later than six months after the FER is due (i.e., no later than 33 months after becoming subject to requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: History of construction requirement (§257.73(c)) for closed-with-waste-in-place units
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must complete the history of construction, providing information on original site conditions, unit design and construction (cross sections, elevations), and subsequent revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: History of construction is used to design/evaluate groundwater monitoring systems, closures, and corrective actions; helps determine whether unit intersects groundwater and informs post-closure care and corrective action decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent marker installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments that closed by removal or with waste in place prior to the effective date must install a permanent marker at the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent marker is a required element of the tailored subsets of requirements to identify the unit and (implicitly) provide information for future monitoring or land-use considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not-applicable design/operational criteria for closed units
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain design and operating criteria (e.g., Emergency Action Plan (EAP), weekly inspections, inflow design flood control plan) are not applicable to units that have closed by removal or to units that have completed closure with waste in place and installed a final cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concluded these criteria primarily address risks from unclosed or operating units; for closed units, post-closure care and monitoring are the relevant obligations instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide closure documentation meeting §257.102(d) or §257.101(g) for closures with waste in place
rubrics_metrics.description: For units that completed closure with waste in place, the final rule requires the facility to provide information on the completed closure and supporting documentation to demonstrate that the closure meets the performance standards in §257.102(d) or the standards in §257.101(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a facility can document that closure meets §257.102(d) performance standards, required obligations reduce to groundwater monitoring in §§257.90–257.95, corrective action as necessary during post-closure care, and recordkeeping/posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral to permitting for certain closure activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule contains a revision allowing deferral of certain closure activities to permitting in specified circumstances (the final rule adds deferral to permitting as an additional revision beyond the proposed rule's four changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Unit III.B.2.g.iii.(b) discussions in preamble for details and conditions under which closure activities may be deferred to permitting; deferral affects which requirements apply immediately versus via permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance deadlines principles and adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance deadlines for legacy CCR surface impoundments are framed relative to the effective date (final rule effective six months after publication) and were extended to provide at least as much time as the 2015 CCR Rule; EPA considered factors such as contractor/laboratory backlogs, seasonality, overlapping regulatory requirements, availability of historical documentation, disposal capacity, and COVID impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA received comments that proposed expedited deadlines were infeasible; in response, EPA reassessed and extended deadlines in many cases. Deadlines reflect practical constraints (mobilization times, permitting coordination, QA/QC needs) and in some cases exceed 2015 CCR Rule timeframes. Facilities thus have an additional six months from publication to comply with deadlines referenced to the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No 'innocent owner' exemption included
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA declined to establish an 'innocent owner' provision in the final rule because the Agency had no factual basis to do so and because most potential legacy impoundments are owned by companies already regulated under CCR regulations; EPA found existing private allocation of liability via agreements sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators should not expect a regulatory innocent-owner exemption; responsibility for compliance remains with the unit owner/operator as allocated by relevant agreements and consistent with the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'inactive facility' and applicability regardless of how electricity is produced
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalized use of October 19, 2015 as the operative date to define an 'inactive facility' and clarified that the rule applies 'regardless of how electricity is currently being produced at the facility' (i.e., coverage applies without regard to the fuel used, including facilities producing electricity via renewables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA rejected commenters' requests for exemptions based on renewable retrofits (including a proposed 50 MW renewable-only exemption) because present operations do not correlate to historic risks from past coal-fired operations; facilities producing electricity through renewables are subject to the same compliance deadlines for legacy units.
